Hello! As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the Dockerfile and the build error you've encountered.

### Error Identification

The build process is failing at this step:
```
RUN cp /app/kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/
```
The error message `cp: cannot stat '/app/kripke/build/kripke': No such file or directory` clearly indicates that the `kripke` executable is not located at the path `/app/kripke/build/kripke` after the compilation step.

Based on the standard build structure of CMake-based projects like Kripke, the compiled executables are typically placed in a `bin` subdirectory within the build folder. The comment in the Dockerfile suggesting otherwise appears to be incorrect.

### Recommended Fix

The solution is to correct the path in the `cp` command to point to the correct location of the executable, which is `/app/kripke/build/bin/kripke`.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Base Image: Use a recent, stable OS like Ubuntu 22.04
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git, and OpenMPI.
# We remove the system 'cmake' and add 'wget' to download a newer version.
# The --no-install-recommends flag reduces image size.
# Installing ca-certificates is crucial for secure network communications.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    make \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a recent version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies (RAJA).
# The version in Ubuntu 22.04's apt repository is too old (3.22.1 < 3.23).
# We download and install the official binary to ensure compatibility.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.7
RUN case $(uname -m) in \
        x86_64) ARCH=x86_64 ;; \
        aarch64) ARCH=aarch64 ;; \
    esac && \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh && \
    ./cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh --skip-license --prefix=/usr/local && \
    rm cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh

# Configure Open MPI for running within a container.
# These settings help prevent common errors related to process launching,
# shared memory access, and network interface selection in containerized environments.
# Oversubscription is enabled to allow flexibility in Kubernetes resource allocation.
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=false \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp

# Clone Kripke and its submodules recursively to satisfy build dependencies like BLT.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /app/kripke

# Create a build directory, configure Kripke with MPI support, and compile it.
# Using -j$(nproc) parallelizes the build to speed up image creation.
RUN mkdir /app/kripke/build && \
    cd /app/kripke/build && \
    cmake \
        -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
        .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# FIX: Copy the compiled executable from the build directory's 'bin' subdirectory to a system location on the PATH.
RUN cp /app/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/

# Clean up the build directory and source code to minimize final image size.
RUN rm -rf /app/kripke

# Set a default working directory for when the container is run.
WORKDIR /data

# Define the default command. Running the container without arguments will
# execute 'kripke' which typically displays the help/usage message.
CMD ["kripke"]
```

    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for running within a container.
# These settings help prevent common errors related to process launching,
# shared memory access (btl_vader), and network interface selection in
# environments like Kubernetes where a scheduler manages resources.
# Oversubscription is enabled to allow flexibility in Kubernetes resource allocation.
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=false \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch

# Create a build directory, configure Kripke with MPI support, and compile it.
# Using -j$(nproc) parallelizes the build to speed up image creation.
RUN mkdir /app/kripke/build && \
    cd /app/kripke/build && \
    cmake \
        -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
        .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# This makes the 'kripke' command directly available to users and scripts.

# execute 'kripke' which typically displays the help/usage message.

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git, and OpenMPI.
# We remove the system 'cmake' and add 'wget' to download a newer version.
# The --no-install-recommends flag reduces image size.
# Installing ca-certificates is crucial for secure network communications.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    make \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a recent version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies (RAJA).
# The version in Ubuntu 22.04's apt repository is too old (3.22.1 < 3.23).
# We download and install the official binary to ensure compatibility.

        x86_64) ARCH=x86_64 ;; \
        aarch64) ARCH=aarch64 ;; \
    esac && \

    chmod +x cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh && \
    ./cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh --skip-license --prefix=/usr/local && \
    rm cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh

# Configure Open MPI for running within a container.
# These settings help prevent common errors related to process launching,
# shared memory access, and network interface selection in containerized environments.
# Oversubscription is enabled to allow flexibility in Kubernetes resource allocation.
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=false \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp

# Clone Kripke and its submodules recursively to satisfy build dependencies like BLT.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /app/kripke

# Create a build directory, configure Kripke with MPI support, and compile it.
# Using -j$(nproc) parallelizes the build to speed up image creation.
RUN mkdir /app/kripke/build && \
    cd /app/kripke/build && \
    cmake \
        -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
        .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# FIX: Copy the compiled executable from the build directory to a system location on the PATH.
# The Kripke executable is located directly in the build directory, not a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /app/kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/

# Clean up the build directory and source code to minimize final image size.
RUN rm -rf /app/kripke

# Set a default working directory for when the container is run.
WORKDIR /data

# Define the default command. Running the container without arguments will
# execute 'kripke' which typically displays the help/usage message.
CMD ["kripke"]

    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \

    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Base Image: Use a recent, stable OS like Ubuntu 22.04
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git, and OpenMPI.
# We add 'wget' to download a newer version of CMake, as the one from apt is too old.
# The --no-install-recommends flag reduces image size.
# Installing ca-certificates is crucial for secure network communications (e.g., git, wget).
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    make \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a recent version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies (e.g., RAJA).
# The version in Ubuntu 22.04's apt repository is too old (3.22.1 < 3.23).
# We download and install the official binary from Kitware to ensure compatibility
# and support for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.7
RUN case $(uname -m) in \
        x86_64) ARCH=x86_64 ;; \
        aarch64) ARCH=aarch64 ;; \
    esac && \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh && \
    ./cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh --skip-license --prefix=/usr/local && \
    rm cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh

# Configure Open MPI for running within a containerized environment like Kubernetes.
# These settings prevent common errors related to process launching,
# shared memory access (btl_vader), and network interface selection.
# Oversubscription is enabled to allow flexibility in Kubernetes resource allocation.
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=false \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is critical to fetch build dependencies like BLT and RAJA.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /app/kripke

# Create a build directory, configure Kripke with MPI support enabled, and compile it.
# Using -j$(nproc) parallelizes the build to speed up image creation.
RUN mkdir /app/kripke/build && \
    cd /app/kripke/build && \
    cmake \
        -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
        .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a directory on the system's PATH.
# The build system places the binary in the 'bin' subdirectory of the build folder.
RUN cp /app/kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/

# Clean up the build directory and source code to minimize final image size.
RUN rm -rf /app/kripke

# Set a default working directory for when the container is run.
WORKDIR /data

# Define the default command. Running the container without arguments will
# execute 'kripke' which typically displays its help/usage message.
CMD ["kripke"]

# Install build dependencies, git, cmake, and OpenMPI.
# The --no-install-recommends flag reduces image size.
# Installing ca-certificates is crucial for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    cmake \
    git \
    make \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for running within a container.
# These settings help prevent common errors related to process launching,
# shared memory access (btl_vader), and network interface selection in
# environments like Kubernetes where a scheduler manages resources.
# Oversubscription is enabled to allow flexibility in Kubernetes resource allocation.
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=false \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /app/kripke

# Create a build directory, configure Kripke with MPI support, and compile it.
# Using -j$(nproc) parallelizes the build to speed up image creation.
RUN mkdir /app/kripke/build && \
    cd /app/kripke/build && \
    cmake \
        -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
        .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a directory on the system's PATH.
# This makes the 'kripke' command directly available to users and scripts.
RUN cp /app/kripke/build/bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/

# Clean up the build directory and source code to minimize final image size.
RUN rm -rf /app/kripke

# Set a default working directory for when the container is run.
WORKDIR /data

# Define the default command. Running the container without arguments will
# execute 'kripke' which typically displays the help/usage message.
CMD ["kripke"]

The comment and the `cp` command in the Dockerfile were based on an incorrect assumption about the output location.

To fix this, the source path in the `cp` command must be corrected to point to `/app/kripke/build/kripke`.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Base Image: Use a recent, stable OS like Ubuntu 22.04
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, git, and OpenMPI.
# We add 'wget' to download a newer version of CMake, as the one from apt is too old.
# The --no-install-recommends flag reduces image size.
# Installing ca-certificates is crucial for secure network communications (e.g., git, wget).
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    make \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install a recent version of CMake required by Kripke's dependencies (e.g., RAJA).
# The version in Ubuntu 22.04's apt repository is too old (3.22.1 < 3.23).
# We download and install the official binary from Kitware to ensure compatibility
# and support for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures.
ENV CMAKE_VERSION=3.27.7
RUN case $(uname -m) in \
        x86_64) ARCH=x86_64 ;; \
        aarch64) ARCH=aarch64 ;; \
    esac && \
    wget https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v${CMAKE_VERSION}/cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh && \
    chmod +x cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh && \
    ./cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh --skip-license --prefix=/usr/local && \
    rm cmake-${CMAKE_VERSION}-linux-${ARCH}.sh

# Configure Open MPI for running within a containerized environment like Kubernetes.
# These settings prevent common errors related to process launching,
# shared memory access (btl_vader), and network interface selection.
# Oversubscription is enabled to allow flexibility in Kubernetes resource allocation.
ENV OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=false \
    OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch.
# The --recurse-submodules flag is critical to fetch build dependencies like BLT and RAJA.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /app/kripke

# Create a build directory, configure Kripke with MPI support enabled, and compile it.
# Using -j$(nproc) parallelizes the build to speed up image creation.
RUN mkdir /app/kripke/build && \
    cd /app/kripke/build && \
    cmake \
        -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
        .. && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled Kripke executable to a directory on the system's PATH.
# The executable is placed directly in the build directory, not a 'bin' subdirectory.
RUN cp /app/kripke/build/kripke /usr/local/bin/

# Clean up the build directory and source code to minimize final image size.
RUN rm -rf /app/kripke

# Set a default working directory for when the container is run.
WORKDIR /data

# Define the default command. Running the container without arguments will
# execute 'kripke' which typically displays its help/usage message.
CMD ["kripke"]
